title: Mapping-complex presentation of an enriched model localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose its classes $C,F,W$ form a model structure: $W$ has two-out-of-three; the classes are retract closed; $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations and generated by sets. Suppose also that, for $i:A\to B$ in $C$ and $p:X\to Y$ in $F$, the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,X)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,Y)$$
is a degreewise surjection of complexes, and a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ belongs to $W$. An object is cofibrant when its initial map is in $C$, fibrant when its terminal map is in $F$, and bifibrant when both hold. Use enriched localization in the sense of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal].

The inclusions of the full differential graded subcategories $\mathcal M_c$, $\mathcal M_f$ and $\mathcal M_{cf}$ of cofibrant, fibrant and bifibrant objects induce equivalences after enriched localization at their inherited weak equivalences. The full bifibrant differential graded category, interpreted with its derived chain enrichment, itself presents $\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$. For cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $I$, the complex $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal M}(P,I)$ represents its enriched mapping object; these identifications are natural as a bifunctor on $\mathcal M_c^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal M_f$, compatible with composition wherever defined. This bifunctor sends weak equivalences in either variable to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus for functorial cofibrant and fibrant replacements $QX\to X$ and $Y\to TY$, a model for the derived mapping object is $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(QX,TY)$. The localized inclusion equivalences and these comparison bifunctors identify different choices with coherent natural equivalences; an enriched choice of the replacement functors is not required.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction at mapping-complex level: comparison of the differential graded model with its enriched localization, an additional agent-formulated foundation absent from this blueprint.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal H(A,B)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal M}(A,B)$. The initial and terminal objects agree: in the underlying preadditive category, the identity of an initial object is its zero endomorphism, so every morphism into it is zero and it is terminal. Write this zero object as $0$. For every complex $K$, the tensor adjunction identifies maps $K\to\mathcal H(P,0)$ with maps $K\otimes P\to0$, a singleton; the cotensor adjunction identifies maps $K\to\mathcal H(0,I)$ with maps $0\to I^K$, also a singleton. Thus both Hom complexes are terminal complexes, hence zero. Apply the assumed mapping axiom to $0\to P$ and $I\to0$. For cofibrant $P$, $\mathcal H(P,-)$ sends trivial fibrations to surjective quasi-isomorphisms; for fibrant $I$, $\mathcal H(-,I)$ sends trivial cofibrations to surjective quasi-isomorphisms. Extend to weak equivalences on the required domains using [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations], with the following explicit argument. For a weak equivalence $u:P\to P'$ between cofibrant objects, its Brown factorization is $u=pi$ with $p:Z\to P'$ a trivial fibration, $i:P\to Z$ a cofibration and $s:P'\to Z$ a cofibration satisfying $ps=1$. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations, and $Z$ is cofibrant. Thus $\mathcal H(i,I)$ and $\mathcal H(s,I)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. The equation $\mathcal H(s,I)\mathcal H(p,I)=1$ makes $\mathcal H(p,I)$ a quasi-isomorphism, and then so is $\mathcal H(u,I)$. For a weak equivalence $v:I\to I'$ between fibrant objects, use the dual Brown factorization $v=pi$ with $i:I\to Z$ a trivial cofibration and $p:Z\to I'$ a fibration admitting a fibration retraction $r:Z\to I$ of $i$. Now $p,r$ are trivial fibrations and $Z$ is fibrant. Hence $\mathcal H(P,p)$ and $\mathcal H(P,r)$ are quasi-isomorphisms, the equation $\mathcal H(P,r)\mathcal H(P,i)=1$ makes $\mathcal H(P,i)$ one, and consequently $\mathcal H(P,v)$ is one. This proves both weak-equivalence invariance assertions for the mixed Hom bifunctor.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; agent-supplied dg-model foundation: Brown argument for mixed Hom invariance

proof.text:
Construct an auxiliary dg category $\mathcal R_c$ whose objects are all trivial fibrations $p:P\to X$ with $P$ cofibrant. Put
$$\mathcal R_c(p,p')=\mathcal H(P,P')\times_{\mathcal H(P,X')}\mathcal H(X,X'),$$
where the two maps are postcomposition by $p'$ and precomposition by $p$. A homogeneous element is a pair $(a,b)$ satisfying $p'a=bp$. Differential and composition are componentwise; for composable pairs, $p''a'a=b'p'a=b'bp$, so composition stays in the pullback and its associativity and units follow from those of $\mathcal M$. There are dg functors $a_c:\mathcal R_c\to\mathcal M_c$, $(P\to X)\mapsto P$, and $\pi_c:\mathcal R_c\to\mathcal M$, $(P\to X)\mapsto X$, with a dg natural transformation $p:j_ca_c\to\pi_c$ whose components are the displayed resolution maps. Here $j_c$ is the inclusion. Declare a closed degree-zero square to belong to $W_c$ exactly when its $X$-component is in $W$; the equation $p'a=bp$ and two-out-of-three say equivalently that its $P$-component is in $W$. Thus both projections preserve the specified weak equivalences.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; agent-supplied dg-model foundation: dg category of all cofibrant resolutions and its two projections

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dg-resolution-square-projection] to $\mathcal A=\mathcal M$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal M$, $\mathcal E=\mathcal M_c$ and the arrows $p:P\to X$ of step 2. Its local hypothesis is exactly the surjective quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal H(P,P')\to\mathcal H(P,X')$ supplied by the mapping axiom for cofibrant $P$ and trivial fibration $p'$. Its object hypothesis follows by factoring $0\to X$. Its square category is precisely $\mathcal R_c$. Its distinguished arrows are precisely $W_c$, since those were defined by their $X$ components. The lemma therefore gives a quasi-equivalence $\pi_c$ and an enhanced equivalence $\overline\pi_c:\mathcal R_c[W_c^{-1}]\simeq\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$, with all coherent diagram comparisons. This isolates the pullback-of-complexes and weak-equivalence-lifting arguments in the cited lemma.

source.place: Agent resolution-square projection for proof paragraph 2

proof.text:
Let $L=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$ and $L_c=\mathcal M_c[W^{-1}]$, and put bars on localized functors. Define $S_c=\overline a_c\,\overline\pi_c^{-1}$. Localizing $p:j_ca_c\to\pi_c$ gives $\overline j_cS_c\simeq1_L$, since its components are weak equivalences. Restrict $\mathcal R_c$ to objects $P\to X$ with $X$ cofibrant, with inclusion $k$ and projection $\pi_c^c$ to $\mathcal M_c$. Apply [lem-coef-dg-resolution-square-projection] again: the same mapping axiom verifies its local hypothesis, and factoring $0\to X$ verifies its object hypothesis even for cofibrant $X$. Hence $\overline\pi_c^c$ is an equivalence. Now $\pi_ck=j_c\pi_c^c$, while the restricted transformation $p$ lies entirely in $\mathcal M_c$ and gives $\overline a_c\,\overline k\simeq\overline\pi_c^c$. Thus
$$S_c\overline j_c\simeq\overline a_c\,\overline k(\overline\pi_c^c)^{-1}\simeq1_{L_c}.$$
The transformations and their diagrams descend by [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. This constructs both enhanced inverse comparisons without choosing a dg replacement functor.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; agent-supplied dg-model foundation: two inverse comparisons for the cofibrant inclusion

proof.text:
For $\mathcal D=\mathcal M$ or $\mathcal M_c$, let $\mathcal E$ consist of its fibrant objects. Let $\mathcal R$ have objects trivial cofibrations $j:X\to I$ with $X\in\mathcal D$ and $I$ fibrant. If $X$ is cofibrant, then $I$ is cofibrant because $0\to X\to I$ is a composite of cofibrations. Thus $I\in\mathcal E$. Put
$$\mathcal R(j,j')=\mathcal H(X,X')\times_{\mathcal H(X,I')}\mathcal H(I,I').$$
The relation $j'b=aj$ is preserved by differential; componentwise composition preserves it since $j''b'b=a'j'b=a'aj$. Apply the dual assertion of [lem-coef-dg-resolution-square-projection]. Its local hypothesis is the mapping axiom for the trivial cofibration $j$ and fibrant $I'$, giving a surjective quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal H(I,I')\to\mathcal H(X,I')$. Factoring $X\to0$ provides an object over each $X$. The source projection $\pi:\mathcal R\to\mathcal D$ is consequently a quasi-equivalence and a localized enhanced equivalence, marking squares by $b\in W$. Two-out-of-three and $j'b=aj$ show equivalently $a\in W$.

source.place: Agent fibrant resolution-square construction for proof paragraph 2

proof.text:
Write $e:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ for inclusion and $a:\mathcal R\to\mathcal E$ for target projection. The dg natural transformation $j:\pi\to ea$ has weak-equivalence components. Set $S=\overline a\,\overline\pi^{-1}$. By [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], localizing $j$ gives $\overline eS\simeq1$. Restrict to objects $j:X\to I$ with $X\in\mathcal E$, with inclusion $k$ and source projection $\pi^{\mathcal E}$. The dual resolution-square lemma applies again: the local hypothesis is still the mapping axiom for $j$ and $I'$, and the factorization of $X\to0$ remains in $\mathcal E$ (and preserves cofibrancy when relevant). Hence $\overline\pi^{\mathcal E}$ is an equivalence. Now $\pi k=e\pi^{\mathcal E}$ and the restricted $j$ lies in $\mathcal E$, so $\overline a\,\overline k\simeq\overline\pi^{\mathcal E}$. Therefore
$$S\overline e\simeq\overline a\,\overline k(\overline\pi^{\mathcal E})^{-1}\simeq1.$$
The cited localization theorem preserves these transformation diagrams. Taking $\mathcal D=\mathcal M$ proves the fibrant inclusion equivalence; taking $\mathcal D=\mathcal M_c$ proves the bifibrant-to-cofibrant inclusion equivalence. Combined with step 4 this gives $\mathcal M_{cf}[W^{-1}]\simeq L$.

source.place: Agent fibrant inverse comparisons for proof paragraph 2

proof.text: Every weak equivalence $w:A\to B$ between bifibrant objects is already an equivalence in their dg category interpreted with derived enrichment. Indeed step 1 makes $\mathcal H(w,A):\mathcal H(B,A)\to\mathcal H(A,A)$ a quasi-isomorphism. On $H^0$, lift $[1_A]$ to a class $[g]$, represented by a closed degree-zero map $g:B\to A$, so $[gw]=[1_A]$. Also $\mathcal H(w,B)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence injective on $H^0$. Since $[(wg)w]=[w]=[1_Bw]$, this injectivity gives $[wg]=[1_B]$. Thus $[g]$ is a two-sided inverse in $H^0$, which is precisely the equivalence condition for a dg category's derived enrichment as in [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda]. In the universal property of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], every enhanced functor from this category already inverts these maps. Its localization is therefore equivalent to itself. Combine with step 6 to obtain the enhanced equivalence $\mathcal M_{cf}\simeq L$ induced by the inclusion.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; agent-supplied dg-model foundation: weak equivalences of bifibrant objects and the unlocalized dg presentation

proof.text:
The localization functor $\ell:\mathcal M\to L$ supplies the canonical comparison
$$\gamma_{P,I}:\mathcal H(P,I)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_L(\ell P,\ell I)$$
in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$, natural on the entire dg bifunctor $\mathcal M_c^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal M_f$. To prove it an equivalence, choose a trivial cofibration $j:P\to J$ with $J$ fibrant. Since $P$ is cofibrant, $J$ is bifibrant. Choose a trivial fibration $p:R\to I$ with $R$ cofibrant. Since $I$ is fibrant, $R$ is bifibrant. The comparisons form commuting squares with
$$\mathcal H(P,I)\xleftarrow{j^*}\mathcal H(J,I)\xleftarrow{p_*}\mathcal H(J,R).$$
The first arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by the mapping axiom for the trivial cofibration $j$ and fibrant $I$. The second is one by the axiom for cofibrant $J$ and the trivial fibration $p$. The corresponding arrows between mapping objects in $L$ are equivalences because $\ell j$ and $\ell p$ are equivalences. Finally $\gamma_{J,R}$ is an equivalence by the fully faithful bifibrant presentation of step 7. The commuting squares and two-out-of-three prove $\gamma_{P,I}$ an equivalence. Hence the original canonical bifunctor comparison is pointwise an equivalence, so is an enhanced natural equivalence by [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Compatibility with composition follows from that of the single enriched functor $\ell$: for cofibrant $P,J$ and fibrant $J,I$, the two routes from $\mathcal H(J,I)\otimes\mathcal H(P,J)$ to the localized mapping object are the images of the same composition map. In derived enrichment these maps use derived tensor, with its canonical map to the ordinary tensor presentation. All higher composition diagrams are the images of the corresponding dg diagrams, not newly chosen objectwise inverses.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; agent-supplied dg-model foundation: mixed mapping comparison and its composition diagrams

proof.text:
For cofibrant replacements $q_X:QX\to X$ and fibrant replacements $t_Y:Y\to TY$, step 8 applied to $(QX,TY)$ gives
$$\mathcal H(QX,TY)\simeq\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_L(\ell X,\ell Y).$$
Explicitly a map $f:\ell QX\to\ell TY$ is sent to $(\ell t_Y)^{-1}f(\ell q_X)^{-1}$. The maps $q_X,t_Y$ need only be weak equivalences with the stated cofibrancy and fibrancy. By step 1 the mixed Hom bifunctor inverts weak equivalences separately in both variables. The multivariable assertion of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] therefore extends the bifunctor, its canonical comparison and the composition diagrams of step 8 along both localized domains. This proves the derived-mapping formula and its enhanced naturality on those domains.

source.place: Agent replacement mapping formula for proof paragraph 2

proof.text: For ordinary functorial factorizations, a strict ordinary indexing diagram of chosen resolutions gives closed degree-zero squares in $\mathcal R_c$ or $\mathcal R$ of step 5, respecting composition. The free $\mathbf Z$-linear category on that indexing category, placed in degree zero, therefore maps by a dg functor to the resolution category. Its localized projection identifies it with the projected diagram. For a general enhanced indexing diagram use [lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance]: steps 3 and 5 give actual quasi-equivalences, so derived pre- and postcomposition induce equivalences of full derived dg functor categories, including transformation objects. Equivalently one may invert the localized projections using [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Lifting a fixed diagram together with its specified projection is a fiber of an equivalence; it is contractible, as is the space of an object with a specified equivalence to a fixed object. This supplies coherent lifts through the resolution spans. It never applies an ordinary replacement functor as a dg functor, and begins with enhanced diagrams rather than just diagrams in $H^0$.

source.place: Agent coherent lifting through resolution spans for proof paragraph 2

proof.text: For another pair $Q',T'$, compare both replacement mapping models to the single mapping bifunctor of $L$ in step 9, and compose one comparison with the inverse of the other. The extension spaces with specified restriction in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] are contractible and compatible with substitution. Thus these comparisons define enhanced natural equivalences on whole diagrams, with their coherent transformations. For three choices the cocycle comparison is obtained by cancelling the middle equivalence with its inverse; higher compatibilities belong to the same contractible extension spaces. Together with the lifts of step 10 this proves the asserted independence of choices without requiring enriched replacement functors.

source.place: Agent coherent independence of replacement choices for proof paragraph 2

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2 motivates the coefficient mapping comparison but contains no general enriched model theorem. The proof here is the explicit dg resolution-square construction, Brown split factorization, and the existing enhanced localization universal property. Stacks Tag 09T5 (derived.tex, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) is only an ordinary-adjunction prototype, not a source for an enriched assertion.
